Rubini, D., Karefyllidis, N., Xu, L., Rosic, B. and Johannesdahl, H. (2022). A new robust regenerative turbo-reactor concept for clean hydrocarbon cracking. Journal of the Global Power and Propulsion Society 6: 135-150. https://doi.org/10.33737/jgpps/150550. Authors at Oxford Thermofluids Institute, Whittle Laboratory (Cambridge) and Coolbrook Oy.

Locators are PRINTED journal page numbers (135-150; PDF page = printed - 134). A turbomachinery CFD design paper (URANS and LES of the rotor/diffuser of Coolbrook's Roto-Dynamic Reactor, RDR): it contains NO energy per tonne of ethylene, no electrical or thermal efficiency, no yields from simulation, no cost and no TRL. Loaded to main (one example, mapped to steam-cracker_electric, which absorbed steam-cracker_rotodynamic on 2026-10-02): description, state-of-development, operating temperature (900-1050 degC) and pressure (1.5-3.0 bar) ranges, and the at-least-70% CO2 reduction from electrification. Qualitative or vendor claims (20% higher ethylene+propylene yield, 5-10x shorter residence time, 500x smaller volume, 200 degC cooler wall, about 290 kJ/kg per stage) are in _other-values because they are not specific energy and the 20% yield is a Coolbrook private communication. Heating-value basis: not applicable (no fuel). The to-get row also wants the AIChE Spring Meeting 2024 paper 120f (integration of the RDR into existing steam crackers), which is the likely source of specific electricity per t ethylene; that is NOT this paper. This paper is also not a source for direct-heater_rotodynamic (the RDH electric heater, AIChE 2023 106a, is a different Coolbrook device).
